permits.limitation: Discovery walks the record-number space by prefix and year, because eTRAKiT publishes no recently-changed feed. A record whose number falls outside the configured prefixes is not discovered.

gis_spatial.limitation: County zoning covers unincorporated Napa County. City of Napa zoning is not published in the county GIS org and is not ingested.

business_openings.limitation: California ABC is a statewide source scoped to Napa (county code 28) and Solano (48) by ABC's own county column, so a jurisdiction with no rows in a given window is a real answer about that window, not a gap. It carries alcohol licensing only: a new restaurant with a licence appears, a retail or office tenant does not. Verified from a residential network; www.abc.ca.gov still answers some datacentre clients with a Cloudflare interactive challenge, and the collector reports that as blocked rather than defeating it.

transportation.limitation: Caltrans state projects plus 511's live traffic and construction events on state routes through the two counties. Events are kept by 511's own county label rather than by a bounding box: this endpoint accepts a bbox parameter and ignores it, so a run that trusted it returned Pescadero and Santa Cruz roadwork as Napa and Solano coverage. The 511 work-zone (WZDx) feed carries no county label and stays in smoke, because a rectangle around these two counties necessarily contains part of Sonoma and would place Santa Rosa lane closures on a Napa map.

blocker.reason: OpenGov Procurement, at procurement.opengov.com. Verified September 13, 2026 from an ordinary residential network: every /portal path answers 403 with cf-mitigated: challenge from Cloudflare, to a self-identifying client and to a browser user agent alike, so the challenge belongs to the vendor rather than to our egress. Every other path on the host serves the application shell, so the portal route is the protected one. The challenge is not defeated. This is now known to be the platform for six of the fourteen jurisdictions, so procurement here turns on one vendor's bot policy rather than on fourteen separate problems. Tenant: cityofnapa.

Unusually rich for this service area: each project carries budget and expenditure to date, phase, category, dates and a written description, all in the city's own words. The fields are authored by the city as a labelled block rather than being Envisio schema columns, so a page that stops carrying its labels counts as a parse failure rather than going quiet. Two of eighty publish no expenditure figure; that is recorded as absent and never as zero.

procurement.limitation: PlanetBids publishes the agency's whole bid history, not only open solicitations, and the stage word is the agency's own: Bidding, Closed, Awarded, Canceled, Award Pending. All 239 are collected. Per-bid detail (address, scope, contact, attachments) is fetched only for the stages named in config, because the API throttles and re-reading a solicitation that closed years ago costs the agency capacity every run; the count skipped is reported. Attachments are recorded by name, size and upload date, with no download URL synthesised from the server path the API exposes.

This is the city's CEQA review page, which is where a Dixon project becomes public: project name, clearinghouse number, location, written proposal and hearing documents. Entries run from 1994 to the present under a single 'under review' heading, so the section label is recorded as a hint and each project's real status is read from its own text.

permits.limitation: Tyler EnerGov Civic Access. Reached only after correcting a wrong conclusion: the city's new Civic Access UI genuinely has record search switched off, but the legacy API is live and needs four tenant headers a browser sends and a hand-built request does not. Without them every payload returns HTTP 500, which is indistinguishable from a retired route. Inspections and licences are deliberately not collected - they are not projects and are 81% of the file. The index serves no offset past 10,000 rows, so a run is a recency window and never the whole file; the agency's own total is reported next to what was kept.

The portal's own configuration advertises anonymous search as enabled and the collector refuses to proceed if that ever changes, rather than hammering a door the city has closed. Discovery is by substring query because the API publishes no usable total - it returns -1 on every page - so the set of queries walked is config and is reported per run.
